claims: A meteor is the streak of light, often called a "shooting star," produced when a meteoroid enters Earth's atmosphere at high speed.
Friction with the air causes the meteoroid to burn up, creating a glowing trail.
Meteoroids are typically tiny dust particles.
Some meteoroids can be larger rocky debris.
Most meteors are caused by small debris from comets or asteroids.
Meteors are seen in the upper atmosphere.
Meteors usually burn up completely before hitting the ground.
Exceptionally bright meteors are known as fireballs.
Fireballs can sometimes be seen in the daytime.
A meteoroid is the rock while still in space.
A meteor is the streak of light seen in the atmosphere.
A meteorite is the piece of debris that survives the journey and hits the ground.
Meteor showers occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by a comet.
